channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Significantly Reduces Poverty Rates Ahead of Schedule
item.description: Uzbekistan is reducing poverty faster than projected, with the rate falling from 17% in 2021 to an estimated 8.9% in 2024, and a target of 4.5% by 2026. This decline is attributed to employment support, entrepreneurship, and land use, alongside reduced inequality.

item.title: Bukhara Region and USA Expand Economic and Tourism Ties
item.description: The Bukhara region of Uzbekistan and the United States are strengthening economic and tourism cooperation. Discussions between regional officials and the US Deputy Chief of Mission focused on investment potential, economic opportunities, tourism resources, and ongoing joint projects in agriculture and education.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Reviews Employment and Income Growth Efforts
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev critically reviewed regional efforts to boost employment and increase public income. A new system assigns regional and district-level responsibilities to khokims and economic complexes to address poverty reduction and income growth directly. Some officials are reportedly still not engaging with communities and businesses on the ground.

item.title: Iran Captures Advanced US Submersible Drone in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran seized an advanced US submersible drone in the Strait of Hormuz, designed for seabed mapping and infrastructure monitoring. The Pentagon stated the captured apparatus was an older, non-classified model, asserting it contained no sensitive data or sophisticated radar.

item.title: Brent Crude Oil Price Surpasses $100 Per Barrel for First Time Since July
item.description: Brent crude oil futures traded above $100 per barrel on September 9, marking the first time since July. The price increase is attributed to renewed tensions between the US and Iran, raising concerns about potential supply disruptions from the Middle East.

item.title: Ipoteka Bank and Uzbekistan's Embassy in Hungary Support Technical Education and Professional Development
item.description: Ipoteka Bank, in collaboration with the Embassy of Uzbekistan in Hungary, is supporting technical education and the professional development of specialists. This initiative aims to enhance skills and foster career growth within the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia preparing zero-tariff free trade agreement
item.description: Uzbekistan and Serbia have begun work on a free trade agreement that will establish zero tariff rates for goods on a mutual basis. The agreement is expected to be finalized and signed soon, creating favorable conditions for Uzbek products in the Serbian market. Officials noted that the economies of both countries are complementary rather than competitive.

item.title: Serbia Plans to Open Embassy in Uzbekistan to Simplify Visa Procedures
item.description: Serbia intends to establish an embassy in Uzbekistan, which could significantly simplify visa application processes for Serbian citizens. The two countries also agreed to prepare an intergovernmental agreement on migration and labor mobility. Serbia expressed interest in attracting skilled Uzbek specialists for the EXPO 2027 construction.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Certify Locally Fed Fish for Uninterrupted Export to Russia
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has been instructed to complete certification procedures for fish raised on domestic feed to ensure uninterrupted export to Russia. The Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry reported this. A ban on imported fish feed is in effect for six months to support local producers.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan to Collaborate on Joint Pharmaceutical Research
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan have signed a memorandum of understanding to conduct joint research in the pharmaceutical sector. Cooperation will include knowledge exchange, promoting mutual trade, developing production facilities, joint research, and participation in international exhibitions. This aims to modernize facilities and introduce innovations.

item.title: China to Continue Fuel and Lubricant Supplies to Kyrgyzstan
item.description: China will continue supplying fuel and lubricants to Kyrgyzstan, stated Chinese Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan Liu Jiangping. The country has been receiving aviation fuel and diesel since a month ago. A temporary visa-free regime for Chinese truck drivers was introduced to ensure economic security and uninterrupted supplies.

item.title: Serbia Plans to Open Embassy in Uzbekistan, Simplifying Visa Procedures
item.description: Serbia plans to open an embassy in Uzbekistan, which will significantly simplify visa application processes for Uzbek citizens. Currently, visa arrangements are made through Astana. This move aims to facilitate travel and diplomatic relations between the two countries.

item.title: Malik Bekturganov Appointed as New Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Malik Bekturganov has officially been appointed as the Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan. The relevant document was signed by President Sadyr Japarov. Previously, Bekturganov served as the First Deputy Prosecutor General.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sees Rise in Citizens Seeking Entry to China After Visa Easing
item.description: A significant increase in Kyrgyz citizens wishing to enter China has been observed following the introduction of transit and visa-free regimes, stated Chinese Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan Liu Jianping. China has simplified visa requirements, leading to a surge in applications.

item.title: Kyrgyz Citizen Detained in Turkey Allowed to Return Home by Court
item.description: A court in Izmir, Turkey, has permitted Kyrgyz citizen Ermek Sabyrzhanov, who was detained on suspicion of links to the Gülen movement, to return to Kyrgyzstan. He was released in court. His wife stated he will return within one to two days. The specific court ruling remains unknown.

item.title: 81st session of UN General Assembly opens in New York
item.description: The 81st session of the UN General Assembly has opened at UN Headquarters in New York. Bangladesh diplomat Halilur Rahman became the new president. UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that restoring trust in the multilateral system is a key task. He emphasized that strengthening international cooperation is crucial to counter global challenges.

item.title: North Korea Constructs New Facilities for Uranium Enrichment at Yongbyon, IAEA Reports
item.description: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has reported that North Korea has built new facilities at its Yongbyon nuclear site. These new structures can accommodate up to 28 cascades of centrifuges for uranium enrichment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Declares 2026 Year of Digitalization and AI, Focusing on Cybersecurity
item.description: Kazakhstan has declared 2026 the Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence, featuring an 'AI Month' from September 23 to October 23. The initiative includes the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum and KazHackStan 2026 cybersecurity conference.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Strengthen State Control Over Energy Sector
item.description: Uzbekistan's "Uzenergoinspeksiya" held a meeting to enhance state control in the energy sector and promote rational energy resource use. Priorities include preventing wasteful consumption, ensuring transparency in control measures, and combating corruption. Tasks were assigned to improve energy saving culture, audits, and digital technology integration in state control processes.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Performance in PISA 2025 Study Highlights Global Decline in Student Achievement
item.description: Uzbekistan presented its results for the PISA 2025 study, which focuses on natural science literacy. Globally, average scores in science, reading, and math have reached their lowest since 2000. The study noted a significant decline in reading literacy skills, particularly information evaluation and critical perception, worldwide.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Gold and Foreign Exchange Reserves Increased by $7.8 Billion in August
item.description: Uzbekistan's gold and foreign exchange reserves rose by $7.8 billion in August, primarily due to an increase in the price of gold. The Central Bank reported that gold exports decreased while accumulation increased, leading to a 12% rise in Uzbekistan's gold reserves over eight months.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Japarov Urges Citizens to Learn from Past Mistakes and Avoid Protests
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has called on citizens to learn from past errors and take responsibility for their words, warning against organizing protests. This marks the second such warning from the president in two months regarding criticism of the authorities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Implement 'Barnahus' System for Child Victims of Violence
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning to implement the 'Barnahus' system, a child-centered model for children who are victims or witnesses of violence. The system aims to provide a safe and coordinated environment, preventing children from repeatedly recounting traumatic experiences to different agencies. This initiative is supported by the Prosecutor General's Office, the National Social Protection Agency, and UNICEF.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Gold and Foreign Exchange Reserves Exceed $72 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan's gold and foreign exchange reserves reached over $72 billion as of September 1, an increase of nearly $7.8 billion. The growth is attributed to a sharp rise in the value of gold reserves, driven by increasing gold prices and a physical increase in gold holdings to a record high since 2013.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Education Ministry Reports Positive Trends in PISA-2025 Results
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Education noted positive dynamics in PISA-2025 results, showing a 30-point increase in reading and 33 points in math and science compared to 2009. The ministry highlighted a rise in students reaching basic functional literacy levels and a decrease in lowest performers, emphasizing the need to address educational inequality.

item.title: Rescuers Recover Body of One of Three Drowned in Charvak Reservoir
item.description: Rescuers found the body of one of three family members who drowned on September 2 in the Charvak Reservoir in the Tashkent region. The incident occurred while they were boating. Search efforts are ongoing, involving personnel from Jizzakh and Sirdaryo regions.

item.title: Nearly 20 tons of cargo from Pakistan denied entry to Kyrgyzstan due to missing labels
item.description: Kyrgyzstan denied entry to 19.6 tons of rice and turmeric imported from Pakistan on September 9. Phytosanitary officials at the Ken-Sai checkpoint discovered the mandatory labeling was absent on the packaging. The consignment was returned to Pakistan in compliance with established phytosanitary requirements to ensure border safety.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan increases self-sufficiency in nine key food staples
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's self-sufficiency in nine socially significant food staples increased in the first half of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, according to the Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry. Domestic production fully covers needs for vegetables, potatoes, and dairy products.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's International Standing Enhanced by Hosting Major Events, Says President
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov stated that hosting major international events has elevated Kyrgyzstan's global standing and regional influence. He cited the SCO summit, SCO Plus meeting, state visits by Chinese and Pakistani leaders, and the World Nomad Games as examples. Japarov noted growing international trust and interest in Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Uzbekistan repatriates 27 citizens for violating migration laws in Sweden and Poland
item.description: Uzbekistan has repatriated 27 citizens who violated migration laws in Sweden and Poland. The charter flight landed in Tashkent on September 9. The repatriation was carried out in cooperation with authorized bodies of Uzbekistan, Sweden, and Poland. Efforts continue to improve legal literacy and prevent migration law violations.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Household debt to banks increased by 18.8% in one year
item.description: Household debt to banks in Uzbekistan has increased by 18.8% over the past year. The majority of these loans were used for purchasing homes. The total outstanding loan balance for the population has grown significantly, indicating increased borrowing for housing.

item.title: Private companies to sell liquefied gas at free prices to residents in Andijan region
item.description: Uzbekistan plans a gradual transition to market principles for supplying liquefied gas to the population, starting with a pilot project in Andijan region. At least two private companies will be allowed to sell gas at free prices alongside the state supplier. This aims to improve service quality and create competition.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy Discusses Increased Funding for SMEs with JICA
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy and Commerce met with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to discuss expanding financing for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The talks focused on increasing access to long-term investment resources and enhancing SME competitiveness. SMEs currently represent 51.4% of Kyrgyzstan's GDP.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan improves food security for nine key products by 2026
item.description: In the first half of 2026, Kyrgyzstan saw increased self-sufficiency in nine essential food products compared to the same period in 2025. Domestic production fully met demand for vegetables, potatoes, and milk. Self-sufficiency rates for meat, eggs, bread, sugar, vegetable oil, and fruits/berries also saw varying degrees of growth.

item.title: Kyrgyz parliament proposes limiting rice imports to support local farmers
item.description: A member of the Kyrgyz parliament has proposed restricting rice imports to aid domestic producers facing falling prices. The deputy also suggested establishing processing facilities, including for pasta, to boost local agricultural product processing and create new markets for farmers. Concerns were raised about imported rice being mixed with local produce.

item.title: Uzbekistan's per capita income growing faster than Kazakhstan's, but gap widens
item.description: Uzbekistan's per capita income is growing faster than Kazakhstan's, but the gap between the two countries is widening, according to a World Bank report. Over the past 20 years, per capita income has increased fivefold in Kazakhstan and sevenfold in Uzbekistan. Despite faster growth in Uzbekistan, the income disparity is increasing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prepares for 2027 presidential election, potential candidates emerge
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will elect its president on January 27, 2027. Incumbent President Sadyr Japarov has stated his intention to run for a second term, noting no restrictions for aspiring candidates. Former MP Ishak Masaliev expressed uncertainty about his candidacy, pending party decision.

item.title: Fourteen individuals detained in Tashkent suspected of involvement in transnational drug network
item.description: Tashkent police have arrested 14 people suspected of links to a transnational criminal organization. The arrests were part of coordinated operations across several districts, involving collaboration with international law enforcement. During the operation, a significant quantity of synthetic drugs was seized.

item.title: Russia may intensify strikes on Ukraine infrastructure this winter, Bloomberg reports
item.description: Russia intends to increase attacks on Ukraine's energy and heating infrastructure this winter, according to Bloomberg, citing European officials. The report suggests Russia may also escalate hybrid attacks and political interference in Europe to weaken support for Kyiv.

item.title: Serbian President Urges Companies to Invest in Uzbekistan's Growing Economy
item.description: Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić encouraged Serbian companies to increase their presence in Uzbekistan's market and develop joint projects in technology, industry, energy, AI, biotech, and mining. He noted Uzbekistan's rapid development and potential for mutual benefit, highlighting the country's dynamic growth and long-term development strategy.
